healthcareSystem: Severely under-resourced public healthcare system. Most facilities lack basic supplies and trained staff. Private clinics in Niamey offer slightly better care but still limited. French-speaking healthcare system.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is extremely limited. Niger has one of the lowest doctor-to-patient ratios in the world. Hospitals in Niamey are the best available but still very basic. Outside the capital, healthcare is virtually nonexistent. Medical evacuation to Europe or North Africa is necessary for serious conditions.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Niamey open 8am-12:30pm and 3pm-6:30pm. Very limited availability outside the capital. Night pharmacies (pharmacie de garde) rotate in Niamey.
pharmacyTips: Buy only from licensed pharmacies — look for the green cross sign. Street vendors sell counterfeit and expired medications. Bring essential medications from home. Pharmacists speak French. Stock is limited and inconsistent.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Many medications dispensed without prescription based on availability. Quality assurance is a concern — buy only from licensed pharmacies.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter in French.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry documentation in French with generic medication names.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter translated into French listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supply for your entire trip — local supply is unreliable.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is absolutely essential. Serious conditions cannot be adequately treated locally. Ensure your policy covers evacuation to Europe or North Africa. Some insurers may have restrictions for Niger — verify before travel.

recommended: Meningococcal meningitis (especially during dry season, December-June)
Malaria prophylaxis (essential — malaria is endemic throughout Niger)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever vaccination is REQUIRED for all travelers. Niger is in the African meningitis belt — meningococcal vaccination strongly recommended. Malaria prophylaxis is essential year-round.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink anywhere in Niger. Use only bottled or thoroughly purified water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in all drinks. Water-borne diseases are a significant risk.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food. Avoid raw vegetables and salads. Peel all fruits yourself. Stick to busy, established restaurants. Avoid street food unless freshly cooked. Wash hands frequently or use hand sanitizer.
medicalTourismNote: Niger is not a medical tourism destination. Travelers requiring significant medical care should plan to leave the country.
metaDescription: Health guide for Niger: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Hôpital National de Niamey
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Basic facilities. French-speaking only. Can be overcrowded.

hospitals.name: Clinique Pasteur
hospitals.notes: Private clinic with better facilities than public hospitals. French-speaking. Preferred by expats and aid workers.

hospitals.name: Clinique Gamkalley
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in Niamey. Reasonable facilities for the region. French-speaking staff.

hospitals.name: Hôpital National Lamordé
hospitals.notes: Second major public hospital. Maternity and general services. Basic by international standards.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics exist in Niamey. None outside the capital.
dentalCare.notes: Dental facilities are basic. Sterilization standards may not meet international norms. Bring a dental first-aid kit.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, Clinique Pasteur in Niamey may be able to help. Consider evacuation for complex procedures.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line available
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are virtually nonexistent for foreigners. No English-speaking therapists available. French-speaking psychiatric services very limited. Use telehealth from your home country.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is nonexistent. Roads are unpaved in many areas.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals lack wheelchair access and accessible facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Private vehicles are the only option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Niger is extremely challenging for travelers with mobility issues. Bring all assistive devices and consider hiring local assistance. Contact your embassy for guidance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available in Niamey.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been lifted. Testing capacity remains limited.

insuranceClaimProcess: Very few facilities provide itemized receipts suitable for insurance claims. Pay cash and collect whatever documentation available. Have receipts translated from French. Contact your insurer before treatment if possible.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Payment in West African CFA franc (XOF). Private clinics are more expensive but offer better care.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for any serious medical condition. Local healthcare cannot handle complex cases. Air evacuation to Europe is the standard route.
